Soojin / team,

I reviewed the materials attached. Below are concise position drafts you can send to Atlas (plain English + legal rationale). Feel free to edit for tone.

1) Sublicensing and DR: Proposed position — "Redwood will not sublicense the Software to third-party customers. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may contract with a designated DR provider to operate a replica of the Customer's environment solely for the purpose of disaster recovery; such DR provider will not have rights to use the Software for any other customers or commercial use and must be bound by equivalent confidentiality & security obligations."
Rationale: preserves our no-sublicense policy while allowing narrowly scoped DR operations. Preserves auditability.

2) Audit cadence & scope: Proposed position — "For private deployments, Customer may request an audit no more frequently than once every 18 months. Audits shall be conducted during regular business hours with at least 30 days' notice, limited to the Customer's relevant environment and records. For hosted environments, Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II reports and reasonable assistance in lieu of onsite audits."
Rationale: balances Atlas's regulatory needs with operational stability and confidentiality of other customers.

3) Escrow alternatives: Proposed position — "Redwood cannot deposit source code into customer-controlled escrow as a standard offering. Alternatives we can offer: (a) third-party escrow of a build artifact under mutually agreed release triggers; (b) a formal contractual commitment to provide operational runbooks and a transition plan; or (c) extended warranty & support credits tied to specified outage scenarios."
Rationale: source escrow is high friction; alternative mitigations often satisfy risk for customers.

Next steps: Soojin — if we agree, send these three bullets back to Emma as a short note. Markus, happy to take a follow-up if their legal insists on source escrow; we may need to escalate to VP-level for an exception or structured escrow (third-party with strict release triggers).

-Priyom

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending Priyom's notes — those help a lot. A few updates from our side after an internal check:

- DR carve-out as drafted looks acceptable in principle, but legal asked that we include a sentence requiring the DR provider to be disclosed and approved (standard simple approval).
- Audit cadence: 18 months is acceptable for production environments; for environments processing PHI we will ask for a single additional audit window in the first 12 months post-go-live. Can Redwood accept that limited window?
- Escrow: our legal team confirmed they prefer a third-party escrow deposit of the last known release plus build instructions. They're open to the release triggers being narrow (bankruptcy, insolvency, or Redwood cessation of support).

We can proceed with a markup pass if Redwood can: (a) add a short DR provider approval clause, (b) accept the single 12-month audit window for PHI environments in addition to the 18-month cadence, and (c) provide a statement of willingness to put a third-party escrow in place under limited release triggers.

If you can confirm these three items in writing by end of day Thurs (our legal would like to start drafting the redline), we can schedule a quick 30-min call Friday to align.
